original.text: gang zag blo yi khyad par gyis/ /rim gyis pa dang cig car ba/ /rim gyis pa yi sman chen 'di/ /cig car ba yi dug chen yin/ /cig car ba yi sman chen 'di/ /rim gyis pa yi dug tu 'gyur/ /des na sbyangs pa'i 'phro can la/ /cig car ba ni bstan par bya/ /sems can dang po'i las can la/ /rim gyis pa 'di bstan par bya/
original.edition: Derge Tengyur (sde dge bstan 'gyur), digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling, Tōh 2331; Wylie by the unit (pyewts)
original.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

paraphrase: Homage to the great Vajradhara. By the difference of persons' minds there are the gradual and the simultaneous: this great medicine of the gradual is great poison for the simultaneous; the great medicine of the simultaneous becomes poison for the gradual. Therefore to one with the residue of (previous) training, teach the simultaneous; to beginner beings, teach this gradual (way).

original.text: dang po nyon mongs gdul ba ni/ /khams kyi rab tu dbye ba bya/ /phung po zhig grol bsgom par bya/ /bla mas bstan pa'i lam gyi ni/ /slob ma yongs su smin bya zhing / /bskyed rim gzhung las shes par bya/ /ngag dben pa dang rlung sgom pa/ /bla ma'i zhal las shes par bya/ /sems la dmigs pa'i man ngag ni/ /bde ba chen po'i man ngag go/ /byang chub sems kyi man ngag ni/ /bla ma'i zhal las shes par bya/ /phyag rgya chen po'i man ngag ni/ /man ngag tshig bsdus dag las shes/ /gtum mo 'od gsal sbyangs pa la/ /sgyu ma lta bu'i lus bsgom pa/
original.edition: Derge Tengyur (sde dge bstan 'gyur), digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling, Tōh 2331; Wylie by the unit (pyewts)
original.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

paraphrase: First, to tame the afflictions, analyse the elements and meditate on the aggregates as disintegrating and liberated; the disciple is fully ripened on the path the guru teaches; the generation stage is learned from the texts; isolation of speech and wind meditation are learned from the guru's mouth; the instruction focusing on mind is the instruction of great bliss; the bodhicitta instruction is learned from the guru; the Mahāmudrā instruction is learned from the concise words; having trained in inner heat and clear light, meditate on the illusion-like body.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

paraphrase: Transference is threefold (upward transference by the manner of the generation stage, by the actual illusion, and by clear light); the text sketches each and says clear-light transference is done at the time of death, leading to nirvāṇa in the bardo.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: rmi lam la yang rnam lnga ste/ /dran dang sgyu mar shes pa dang / /sbyangs dang goms pa khrid pa dang / /gong du 'pho bar shes par bya/ /dran pa shes bya sgom pa ni/ /gnyid ma log pa'i dus su yang / /'dun pa dag ni sngon btang ste/ /log ka ma yi shes pa ni/ /dran pas yang dang yang bsgug la/ /bsgugs pas log pa lan re bzhin/ /rab 'bring sad dus 'byung bar 'gyur/
original.edition: Derge Tengyur (sde dge bstan 'gyur), digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling, Tōh 2331; Wylie by the unit (pyewts)
original.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

paraphrase: Dream too has five aspects: recollection, knowing (it) as illusion, training, habituation, and transferring upward. For recollection: even before falling asleep, set the intention and with mindfulness watch again and again for the knowing that is falling asleep; as one falls asleep each time, (recognition) arises on waking for the best and middling.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: de ltar dran pa brtan gyur nas/ /sgyu ma dag tu shes bya ste/ /ma log pa yi dus su yang / /snang srid sgyu mar shes bya ste/ /sgyu ma dngos ni rmi lam yin/ /'di nyid sgyu mar ma shes pas/ /bar do sgyu mar ma shes na/ /bar do'i srid pa mi khegs pas/ /skye ba yang nas yang blangs te/ /khams gsum 'khor bar 'khyams pa yin/
original.edition: Derge Tengyur (sde dge bstan 'gyur), digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling, Tōh 2331; Wylie by the unit (pyewts)
original.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

paraphrase: When mindfulness is stable, know (dreams) as illusion; even when not asleep, know appearance and existence as illusion — the actual illusion is the dream. If this is not known as illusion, and the bardo is not known as illusion, the becoming of the bardo is not blocked; one takes birth again and again and wanders in saṃsāra's three realms.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: yang dang yang goms pas/ /rmi lam byin gyis rlob pa yin/ /de yis bar do rlobs par 'gyur/ /gong ma'i rmi lam goms pa yis/ /'chi ka'i shes pa gsal byas te/ /'chi ka'i rtags rnams tshang ba dang / /sngar goms pa la sems bzhag ste/ /'od gsal bar ni 'jug par bya/ /'chi khar gnyid ni log pa ni/ /dran pa dag na sngon btang nas/ /'od gsal ngang la gnas par bya/
original.edition: Derge Tengyur (sde dge bstan 'gyur), digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling, Tōh 2331; Wylie by the unit (pyewts)
original.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

paraphrase: By habituating again and again, dream is blessed, and by that the bardo is blessed. Through the habituation of dream, making the knowing at death clear: when the signs of death are complete, set the mind in what was trained before and enter clear light; at death, the falling asleep — with mindfulness set beforehand — rest in the state of clear light.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan
notes: The ref is the folio line where the passage begins mid-line.

original.text: sa bon skye gnas rim khyab pa/ /gzhi dang khang pa nyid dang ni/ /las dang sbyor ba rang nus la/ /rang gi ngo bo thig ler bcas/ /bcu gnyis mtha' yi tshig gi don/ / gang gis rtag tu goms gyur nas/ /des ni dngos grub bde ba yi/ /rdo rje 'dzin pa rang nyid 'gyur/ /snang ba thim dang rtog pa thim/ /rags pa thim dang phra ba thim/ /thim pa'i rjes la goms pa dang / /rang bzhin gyis ni 'od gsal 'byung / /de yi rjes la zung 'jug sku/ /slob pa dang ni mi slob gnyis/ /mi slob pa ru gyur pa na/ /'bras bu thob ces bstan pa yin/

paraphrase: (After a list of twelve terms — seed, birthplace, sequence, pervasion, ground, house, action, union, own power and own essence with the bindu — whoever always grows familiar with them becomes the vajra-holder of the siddhi of bliss.) Appearance dissolves, thought dissolves, coarse and subtle dissolve; by familiarity after dissolution natural clear light arises, then the body of union, learner and non-learner; on becoming a non-learner the fruit is said to be attained.

notes: The ref is the folio line where the passage begins mid-line.

original.text: sngon byung srid pa'i sha tshugs can/ /las kyi rdzu 'phrul shugs dang ldan/ /bar do de yi mig snga ru/ /thabs dang shes rab mthong ba la/ /bla ma dag tu dmigs byas te/ / gsang ba'i dbang ni dran byas nas/ /mig ser zhe sdang kun spangs te/ /bde ba'am mi rtog pa bsgoms pa'am/ /yang na sngar dus gang bsgoms pa'i/ /sbyangs pa sngon du dran par bya/ /dus su dran par gyur nas ni/ /dang po'i srid pa khegs par 'gyur/ /de nas bdun phrag bdun gyi bar/ /gong ma bzhin du goms byas na/ /bzhi bcu rtsa dgu 'das pa dang / /'khor ba'i srid pa khegs pa dang / /de ltar sgyu mar gnas pa la/ /'od gsal pa yis sbyang bya ste/ /'od gsal bar ni 'jug par 'gyur/

paraphrase: The being of the intermediate state, with the form of its former existence and the power of karmic miracles: when it sees method and wisdom (a couple in union) before its eyes, it should regard them as the guru, recall the secret empowerment, abandon jealousy and hatred, and meditate on bliss or non-thought, or recall what it trained in before; recalling in time, the first becoming is blocked; thereafter, practising as above for seven weeks, when the forty-nine (days) pass, becoming in saṃsāra is blocked; abiding thus in illusion, purify by clear light and enter clear light.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (Sanskrit/Apabhraṃśa original not extant or not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan
